title: Har with the supine
description: Say what you have done in Swedish: har plus the supine, and when to use it instead of the past.

guide.summary: The Swedish perfect is har plus a special verb form called the supine: jag har ätit, I have eaten. Har never changes, the supine follows the verb group, inte and words like redan and aldrig go right after har, and a fixed past time such as igår takes the simple past instead.

sections.title: Har plus the supine
sections.text: The perfect has two parts: har, the present of ha, and the supine of the main verb. Har is the same for every person, just like every Swedish present form. Swedish never uses är as a helper here, even for gå or komma.
steps: Write har, whatever the subject.
Find the verb's supine: the third form in the deck note (skriver, skrev, skrivit).
Put the supine after har, and the rest of the sentence after it.

examples.sv: Vi har köpt en ny bil.
examples.en: We have bought a new car.

watch: Never är: Hon har kommit, not Hon är kommit.
Har is the same for everyone: de har, not a plural form.
The supine is not the past: har skrev is wrong, har skrivit is right.

sections.title: Supines of regular verbs: -at, -t, -tt
sections.text: Regular verbs build the supine from their past form. Take the past, drop -de, -te or -dde, and add the matching ending. The deck note always shows the supine as its third form.

rows: -er verbs after k, p, s, t

steps: Look at the present: -ar, -er, or a short verb ending in a vowel plus -r.
An -ar verb ends in -at: pratat, jobbat, städat.
An -er verb ends in -t: stängt, köpt, ringt.
A short verb ends in -tt: bott, trott.

examples.en: We have lived here for a long time.

watch: The supine ends in -t, never -d: har stängt, not har stängd. Stängd is the adjective, as in dörren är stängd.
Ringa, köra and höra are -er verbs: ringt, kört, hört, not ringat.

sections.title: Strong and irregular supines
sections.text: Strong verbs change their vowel in the past and end in -it in the supine, often with yet another vowel. A handful of everyday verbs are irregular. Learn these with the verb: the deck note gives all three forms.
steps: If the past changes the vowel (åt, drack, skrev), expect a supine in -it.
Check the vowel in the deck note: dricka gives druckit, not drickit.
Short irregular verbs end in -tt or -t: gått, sett, fått, gjort, haft.
watch: Ha takes its own supine: jag har haft, I have had.
In speech you hear har vart; write har varit.
Gjort and gått have no -it, even though göra and gå are irregular.

sections.title: Inte goes after har
sections.text: In a main clause the first verb comes second, and inte follows that first verb. In the perfect the first verb is har, so inte sits between har and the supine.
steps: Find har, the verb in second place.
Put inte straight after it.
Finish with the supine and the rest of the sentence.

examples.en: We have not tidied the flat.

watch: Jag inte har ätit is the order of a subordinate clause; in a main clause inte follows har.
Inte never goes at the end: Jag har ätit inte is wrong.

sections.title: Just, redan, aldrig, någonsin
sections.text: Small adverbs about time sit in the same slot as inte: right after har, before the supine. English puts them in the same place, so I have already eaten maps straight onto jag har redan ätit.

rows: Jag har aldrig varit i Japan.

steps: Write the subject and har.
Put the adverb directly after har; in a question, after the subject: Har du någonsin.
Then the supine.

examples.en: I have already bought the tickets.

examples.sv: Har du någonsin varit i Norge?
examples.en: Have you ever been to Norway?

watch: Not before har: Vi aldrig har sett snö is wrong.
Någonsin is for questions; in a statement say aldrig.

sections.title: Perfect or past?
sections.text: Use the perfect when no finished time is named: experiences in your life, and results that matter now. As soon as the sentence names a finished time, igår, förra veckan, klockan tolv, use the simple past, the preteritum. This matches English: I have seen it, but I saw it yesterday.
steps: Look for a finished time: igår, förra året, i somras, klockan tolv.
If there is one, use the past: åt, köpte, var.
If there is none and you mean ever, so far or now, use har plus the supine.

examples.sv: Jag har aldrig ätit pizza här.
examples.en: I have never eaten pizza here.

watch: Jag har köpt en bil igår is wrong, just as I have bought a car yesterday is.
Igår first means the verb comes next: Igår köpte jag, not Igår jag köpte.

steps: Write har for every subject.
Add the supine, the third form in the deck note.
Never use är or the past form after har.
Find the group from the present: -ar, -er or a short verb.
-ar gives -at, -er gives -t, a short verb gives -tt.
Keep the -t: the supine never ends in -d.
A vowel change in the past points to a supine in -it.
Check the supine vowel in the deck note.
Learn the irregular ones: varit, haft, gjort, gått, sett, fått.
Find har in second place.
Put inte right after har.
Then the supine.
Put just, redan, aldrig or någonsin right after har.
In a question, put the adverb after the subject: Har du någonsin.
Use någonsin in questions and aldrig in statements.
Look for a finished time such as igår or förra veckan.
A named finished time takes the past.
No time named, and you mean ever or a result now: use har plus the supine.

exercises.hint: Har plus the third form of skriver, skrev, …
exercises.feedback: The perfect is har plus the supine.
exercises.explanation: Jag har skrivit: har, then the supine skrivit.

mistakes.why: Skrev is the simple past. After har the verb takes its supine, the third form in the deck note.
Skriva is a strong verb, so its supine does not take the -at of regular -ar verbs.
That is the simple past, I wrote. The perfect needs har as well.

exercises.hint: Har does not change for vi. Prata is an -ar verb.
exercises.explanation: Vi har pratat: har is the same for every subject, and an -ar verb ends in -at.

mistakes.why: Pratade is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
Swedish builds the perfect with har only, never with är.
That is the simple past, we talked. The perfect needs har in front of the supine.

exercises.hint: Which word helps every Swedish perfect?
exercises.explanation: Hon har läst boken: har plus the supine läst.

mistakes.why: Swedish never builds the perfect with är, unlike French or German with some verbs.
Haft is the supine of ha, had. The helper here has to be the present form.

exercises.hint: The helper is the present of ha, the same for every person.
exercises.explanation: Vi har köpt en ny bil: har does not change for vi.

mistakes.why: Swedish never uses är as the helper of the perfect.
Haft is the supine of ha. The helper must be its present form.
Ha is the infinitive. After vi the verb needs its present form.

exercises.hint: Subject, har, supine, then the object.
exercises.feedback: One tile is a helper Swedish never uses in the perfect.
exercises.explanation: De har ätit lunch: har plus the supine ätit.

mistakes.why: Swedish builds every perfect with har; är cannot help another verb this way.

exercises.hint: Only the subject changes.
exercises.feedback: Har is the same for every person.
exercises.explanation: De har städat rummet: Swedish verbs never change for person, so har stays.

mistakes.why: Städade is the simple past. The supine after har stays as it was.
Hade makes it had tidied, a different tense. Only the subject was meant to change.

answers: Hon har ringt till sin mamma.
exercises.hint: Har plus the supine of ringa, an -er verb. Her own mum is sin.
exercises.explanation: Hon har ringt sin mamma: har, the supine ringt, and sin because the mum is her own. Ringt till sin mamma is also fine.

mistakes.why: Ringde is the simple past. After har the verb takes its supine.
Ringa is an -er verb (ringer), so its supine has no -a- before the -t.
Hennes would mean another woman's mum. Her own mum after the subject hon is sin.

exercises.hint: Bo is a short verb: bor, bodde, …
exercises.explanation: Ni har bott: bo is a short verb, so the supine ends in double t.

mistakes.why: The supine never ends in -d. Short verbs double the t instead.
Bodde is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
Short verbs double the t in the supine; one t is not enough.

exercises.hint: Stänga is an -er verb: stänger, stängde, …
exercises.explanation: Hon har stängt: stängde loses -de and takes -t.

mistakes.why: Stängd is the adjective, as in dörren är stängd. After har the form ends in -t.
Stänga is an -er verb (stänger), not an -ar verb, so no -at.
Stängde is the simple past. After har you need the supine.

exercises.hint: Köper, köpte, …
exercises.explanation: Jag har köpt kaffe: köpa is an -er verb, supine köpt.

mistakes.why: Köpte is the simple past. After har the verb takes its supine.
Köpa is an -er verb (köper), so it does not take the -at of -ar verbs.
-it belongs to strong verbs that change their vowel. Köpa is regular.

exercises.row: -er verbs after k, p, s, t

exercises.hint: Bo is a short verb.
exercises.feedback: Short verbs take -tt in the supine.
exercises.explanation: Vi har bott här länge: we have lived here for a long time, and still do.

mistakes.why: Bodde is the simple past. After har the verb takes its supine.
The supine never ends in -d; a short verb doubles the t.

exercises.hint: The supine never ends in -d.
exercises.explanation: Han har jobbat hela dagen: -ar verbs take -at after har.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. A form ending in -d is an adjective, not the form that follows har.
Jobbade is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
The supine cannot stand alone in a main clause; keep har.

exercises.hint: Ringa is an -er verb: ringer, ringde, …
exercises.explanation: Jag har ringt Erik: ringde loses -de and takes -t. Ringt till Erik is also fine.

mistakes.why: Ringa is an -er verb (ringer), so it does not take the -at of -ar verbs.
Ringde is the simple past. After har the verb takes its supine.
That is the simple past, I called. The English says I have called.

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the perfect.
exercises.hint: Add har and change pratar to its supine.
exercises.explanation: Vi har pratat med Anna: har, then pratat.

mistakes.why: Pratar is the present. After har the verb takes its supine.
Pratade is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
That is the simple past. The perfect needs har.

exercises.hint: Dricker, drack, … The supine has a third vowel.
exercises.explanation: Du har druckit: the vowel changes to u and the ending is -it.

mistakes.why: Drack is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
The vowel changes in the supine as well: check the third form in the deck note.
Strong verbs end in -it in the supine; -at belongs to -ar verbs.

exercises.hint: Gör, gjorde, … Irregular, and no -it.
exercises.explanation: Vi har gjort: göra is irregular, with gj- in the past and the supine.

mistakes.why: Gjorde is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
Gjord is the adjective form, as in läxan är gjord. After har the form ends in -t.
Göra keeps gj- in the supine, just as in the past.

exercises.hint: Är, var, …
exercises.explanation: De har varit: the supine of vara ends in -it.

alternatives.message: Har vart is very common in speech, but write har varit.
De har vart is very common in speech, but write de har varit.

mistakes.why: Var is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
Even vara takes har in the perfect, never är.

exercises.hint: Ser, såg, … A short irregular verb.
exercises.explanation: Har du sett filmen? The supine of se ends in double t.

mistakes.why: Såg is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
The supine of se doubles the t.
Sedd is the adjective form. After har the supine ends in -t.

exercises.hint: Skriver, skrev, …
exercises.explanation: Lars har skrivit ett långt mejl: the strong supine skrivit.

mistakes.why: Skrev is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
-at belongs to -ar verbs. Skriva is strong and changes its vowel in the past.
-t alone belongs to regular -er verbs. Strong verbs end in -it.

exercises.hint: Äta is strong: äter, åt, …
exercises.explanation: Vi har ätit middag: a strong verb takes -it in the supine.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. -at belongs to -ar verbs, and äta is strong.
Åt is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
Äta is not a short verb; its supine ends in -it.

exercises.hint: Har plus the supine of vara.
exercises.explanation: Jag har varit sjuk: har, then varit.

alternatives.message: Har vart is common in speech, but write har varit.

mistakes.why: Var is the simple past. After har you need the supine.
Swedish builds the perfect with har, even for vara.

exercises.hint: Tar, tog, … Which form goes after har?
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the simple past.
exercises.explanation: Han har tagit bilen: ta is strong, supine tagit.

mistakes.why: Tog is the simple past. After har you need the supine.

exercises.hint: Inte follows the verb in second place.
exercises.feedback: Inte goes between har and the supine.
exercises.explanation: Jag har inte ätit: har is second, inte follows it.

mistakes.why: That is subordinate-clause order. In a main clause inte follows the verb in second place.

exercises.hint: Which verb is in second place?
exercises.explanation: Vi har inte sett filmen: har is second, inte comes right after it.

mistakes.why: Inte before the verb is subordinate-clause order. In a main clause the verb comes second and inte follows it.

exercises.hint: Find har and add inte after it.
exercises.feedback: Inte sits between har and the supine.
exercises.explanation: Hon har inte ringt: har, inte, then the supine.

mistakes.why: Inte before the verb is subordinate-clause order, not a main clause.
Inte does not go at the end; it follows the verb in second place.

exercises.hint: The verb comes second in a main clause.
exercises.explanation: Jag har inte gjort läxan: har second, inte after it.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. In a main clause inte follows the verb in second place.
Inte belongs before the supine, straight after har.

exercises.source: We have not tidied the flat.
exercises.hint: Städa is an -ar verb. Inte follows har.
exercises.explanation: Vi har inte städat lägenheten: inte after har, and städat ends in -at.

mistakes.why: In a main clause inte follows the verb in second place.
Städade is the simple past. After har you need the supine.

exercises.instruction: Write the Swedish word for not.
exercises.hint: The word for not goes right after har.
exercises.feedback: Inte sits between har and the supine.
exercises.explanation: De har inte kommit hem: they have not come home.

mistakes.why: Ingen means no or nobody before a noun. To deny a verb, Swedish uses another word.
Aldrig means never. The instruction asks for plain not.

exercises.hint: Redan takes the same place as inte.
exercises.explanation: Filmen har redan börjat: the film has already started.

mistakes.why: In a main clause the verb comes second, so nothing can stand between the subject and har.

exercises.hint: The perfect does not go with a finished time.
exercises.explanation: Har du någonsin varit i London? asks about any time in your life, so the perfect fits.

mistakes.why: Igår names a finished time, and a finished time takes the simple past, not har.
Förra året is a finished time, which needs the simple past, not the perfect.

exercises.instruction: Write the Swedish word for never.
exercises.hint: In a statement, never is one short word after har.
exercises.explanation: Jag har aldrig varit i Japan: aldrig in the slot of inte.

mistakes.why: Någonsin means ever and belongs in questions. The instruction asks for never.
Inte means not. The instruction asks for never.

exercises.source: Have you ever been to Norway?
answers: Har du någonsin varit i Norge?
exercises.hint: Har first, then the subject, then ever.
exercises.explanation: Har du någonsin varit i Norge? In a question the adverb follows the subject.

answers: Har du aldrig varit i Norge?
mistakes.why: Aldrig means never: that asks have you never been. The English asks ever.

exercises.hint: Just takes the slot of inte.
exercises.explanation: Hon har just kommit hem: she has just come home.

mistakes.why: Nothing can stand between the subject and the verb in second place.
Just belongs right after har, before the supine.

exercises.hint: The verb comes second.
exercises.explanation: Vi har aldrig sett snö: har second, aldrig after it.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. In a main clause nothing comes between the subject and har.
Aldrig belongs before the supine, straight after har.

exercises.source: I have already bought the tickets.
exercises.hint: Redan right after har. Köpa gives köpt.
exercises.explanation: Jag har redan köpt biljetterna: redan in the slot after har.

mistakes.why: In a main clause the verb comes second; the adverb follows it.
Redan goes before the supine, straight after har.
Köpte is the simple past. After har you need the supine.

exercises.hint: Igår names a finished time.
exercises.feedback: A finished time takes the simple past.
exercises.explanation: Igår åt jag pizza: yesterday is over, so preteritum.

mistakes.why: The perfect cannot go with a finished time such as igår, just as English cannot say I have eaten yesterday.

exercises.hint: Is a finished time named?
exercises.feedback: Last summer is over: simple past.
exercises.explanation: Förra sommaren var vi i Italien: a named finished time takes preteritum.

mistakes.why: Förra sommaren is a finished time, and the perfect never goes with one.

exercises.instruction: Write äta in the right tense.
exercises.hint: Klockan tolv is a fixed point in the past.
exercises.feedback: A fixed time takes the simple past.
exercises.explanation: Jag åt lunch klockan tolv: a named time, so preteritum.

mistakes.why: Klockan tolv pins the meal to a finished time, and the perfect does not go with one.
Äter is the present. The meal is over.

exercises.instruction: Write vara in the right tense.
exercises.hint: No time is named: this is life experience.
exercises.feedback: Experience with no time named takes the perfect.
exercises.explanation: Jag har varit i Norge många gånger: many times so far in my life.

alternatives.message: Har vart is common in speech, but write har varit.

mistakes.why: The simple past needs a finished time. Here the speaker counts visits up to now.
Var is the simple past. After har you need the supine.

answers: Jag köpte en bil i går.
I går köpte jag en bil.
exercises.hint: Yesterday is a finished time.
exercises.explanation: Jag köpte en bil igår: a named finished time takes preteritum. Igår can also start the sentence: Igår köpte jag en bil.

answers: Jag har köpt en bil igår.
mistakes.why: The perfect does not go with a finished time such as igår.
When igår starts the sentence, the verb must still come second, before the subject.

exercises.hint: No time named: har plus the supine of se.
exercises.feedback: A question about experience takes the perfect.
exercises.explanation: Har du sett filmen? No time is named, so the perfect.

mistakes.why: That asks about one particular showing, did you see it then. The English asks whether you have seen it at all.
Såg is the simple past. After har you need the supine.

exercises.hint: Igår names a finished time.
exercises.feedback: Use the simple past with igår.
exercises.explanation: Jag träffade Anna igår: a finished time takes preteritum.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The perfect cannot go with igår.
Har with a past form is never right, and igår needs the simple past alone.
